title: 4D-STEM in situ Analysis of Nanomaterials at JM
content: Exploring nanostructured materials with atomic resolution using (scanning) transmission electron microscopy ((S)TEM) has become routine for unveiling their structural and electronic properties, which are crucial for understanding reactivity. A deeper and more robust understanding of reaction mechanisms is achieved by imaging catalyst dynamics in their active state, typically at high temperatures and pressures in liquid or gas environments. This approach is central to Johnson Matthey's research on designing improved catalytic materials.
